lux_001: You can recognise it by its trunk forking about three metres up into ten strong branches, spreading like a candelabra. It stands in Square Robert-Brasseur, opposite the Grand Theatre.
lux_002: You can recognise it as the most imposing ginkgo of its kind recorded in the country. It stands in the park of the former Villa Weber, Place Dargent.
lux_003: You can recognise it by its lopsided crown, full over the valley on one side and cramped against the fortress wall on the other, with braced branches. It stands below Bastion Beck.
lux_004: You can recognise it by its new leaves opening translucent red in April and May, darkening to near-black by August. It stands in Parc Pescatore.
lux_006: You can recognise it by the metal cage fitted around its trunk since 2008, its naming plaque now fixed to the cage. It stands in Parc Pescatore.
lux_008: You can recognise it by standing at the Hollerich end of the Petrusse valley path, past the braced beech under Bastion Beck. It stands on the Hollerich section of the path.
lux_010: You can recognise it by standing in Parc Louvigny, within a twenty minute walk of both the giant sequoia in Parc Amelie and the Hollerich sycamore.
